content_voiceover: This slide reviews two board style questions on myeloproliferative neoplasms. Question 11 asks which statement about MPN is not correct, and the answer is A, the driver mutations are not the same across PV, ET, and MF, since although JAK2, CALR, and MPL mutations overlap across all three entities, their frequencies differ substantially, and importantly, triple negative disease, meaning none of the three, is essentially only seen in ET and MF, not PV, since a JAK2 mutation is required for essentially all PV cases. Options B through E are all true, ET does have the best survival among the three MPNs, transplant is not used in low risk disease, watchful waiting is reasonable for low risk asymptomatic patients, and ruxolitinib can be considered even in select low risk symptomatic patients. Question 19 asks which statement about genetic changes in myeloid neoplasms is wrong, and the answer is E, CSF3R mutation is actually strongly associated with chronic neutrophilic leukemia, not chronic myelomonocytic leukemia, which is instead characterized by mutations in genes like SRSF2, TET2, and ASXL1. The other options are correct, SETBP1 and ETNK1 mutations do characterize atypical CML, SF3B1 mutation is classic for MDS slash MPN with ring sideroblasts and thrombocytosis, and JAK2 V617F is strongly linked to polycythemia vera.
keypoints: Q11 answer A, driver mutation frequencies differ across PV, ET, and MF, not identical
Triple negative disease occurs in ET and MF but essentially never in PV
Q19 answer E, CSF3R mutation defines CNL, not CMML
SETBP1 and ETNK1 for atypical CML; SF3B1 for MDS/MPN-RS-T; JAK2 V617F for PV
keypoint_voiceover: Two quick genetics pearls. First, driver mutation frequencies differ across PV, ET, and MF, and triple negative status essentially rules out PV since a JAK2 mutation drives nearly all PV cases. Second, know your genotype phenotype pairs, CSF3R with chronic neutrophilic leukemia, SETBP1 and ETNK1 with atypical CML, SF3B1 with MDS slash MPN with ring sideroblasts and thrombocytosis, and JAK2 V617F with polycythemia vera.
